t: 2114. Maximum Number of Words Found in Sentences
o: Each sentence is words separated by single spaces with no leading/trailing spaces, so the word count is simply the number of spaces plus one (or the result of splitting on spaces). Scan all sentences and take the maximum. Constraints are tiny (<=100 sentences of <=100 chars), so any linear scan works. Example 1: the third sentence has 5 spaces hence 6 words, the maximum.
k: Splitting on a single space is equivalent and equally simple.

a.i: Since separation is exactly one space with no leading/trailing spaces, counting space characters gives words - 1.
s: For each sentence count the spaces and add 1.
Return the maximum over all sentences.
a.t: O(total characters) — each character is examined once

a.i: Splitting on the space character produces exactly the words, so the answer is the maximum split length.
a.t: O(total characters) — splitting touches every character once
a.sp: O(L) per sentence for the split tokens

w: Both approaches are equivalent here; counting spaces avoids allocating token arrays. Pitfall: this relies on the guarantee of no leading/trailing/double spaces — mention that assumption in an interview. Follow-up: what if spacing could be irregular — then split on whitespace with regex or a manual tokenizer.
